Reading this brought back a very specific feeling.

I’ve been in crypto 13 years, long enough to watch things arrive looking like the future and leave without anyone announcing they were gone.

Late 2017 I was flipping cryptokitties almost every day while eth went straight up. I explained them at dinner, to grown adults, and I probably sounded insane, but I wasn’t talking about cartoon cats. 

I thought I was looking at the beginning of digital ownership, culture moving onchain, and a new kind of internet where users could actually own the things they created and collected.

I didn’t think I had caught a mania.

I thought I had seen the future a little earlier than everyone else.

Then 2018 came and robbed me blind… the money disappeared fast. But the belief took years to die.

And even then, it didn’t really die.

It just kept coming back wearing new clothes. NFTs, creator economy, socialfi, onchain social, creator coins. Not all of them were the same, obviously, but somewhere underneath them was a future I had already wanted to believe in once.

That’s why the ideas that hurt the most when they die are rarely the obvious scams. 

Nobody mourns those.

It’s the BEAUTIFUL ones, the ones that made sincere people think, “if this works, crypto actually changes the world.”

You don’t just invest in those ideas! You build your life around them! You make friends through them, attach your name to them, spend years defending them, and start living inside a future that hasn’t arrived yet!!

Then one day the market goes somewhere else.

Usually there’s no dramatic ending. The users stop showing up. The group chats get quieter. The people who used to post about it every day slowly move on. The thesis still sounds beautiful when you say it out loud, it’s just that nothing is walking toward it anymore.

You’re the last one standing in a room explaining what it was supposed to become.

That’s a hard thing to admit, especially in public.

Because you’re burying years of conviction, relationships, reputation, and a version of yourself that genuinely believed you were helping build what came next.

Reading @jessepollak’s post today reminded me I’ve watched this happen over and over again, to other people and to myself.

People outside crypto think the hardest losses are financial.

After enough cycles, you realize some of the hardest losses are the stories you had to stop believing, and the futures you had already started living in.

I still don’t know if I’ve fully let go of all of mine.

Probably not.

1⃣以太坊升级是什么？

以太坊升级是对以太坊网络本身技术上的升级，旨在提升以太坊本身的去中心化、安全性与可扩展性，从而让以太坊更实用。

EIP 是 Ethereum Improvement Proposal 的缩写，是社区关于以太坊改进提议，帮助以太坊进化的提议措施。

2⃣历史上的升级主要做了什么？

柏林升级 —— 柏林升级优化了某些以太坊虚拟机操作的燃料成本，并增加了对多种交易类型的支持。

伦敦升级 —— 伦敦升级引入了 EIP-1559(opens in a new tab)，对交易费市场进行了改革，同时还对燃料费的退款处理方式和冰河世纪日程进行了修改

巴黎升级 —— 以太坊由 POW（工作量证明）转为 POS （权益证明），提升了网络安全性同时更加环保，以太坊目前最重要的一次升级

上海升级 ——上海升级将质押提款引入执行层。 上海升级与卡佩拉升级同时进行，使区块能够接受提款操作，因此质押人可以将以太币从信标链提取到执行层。

坎昆升级 —— 将 Calldata 替换为 Blob 数据类型，显著降低了以太坊 Layer2 的交易费用

3⃣什么是 Pectra （布拉格）升级？

Prague 和 Electra 升级本来最初是单独推出的，但后来合并为一个升级——Pectra——以提高效率和协同作用

Pectra 升级包括对以太坊网络的执行层（智能合约和 dapp 运行的地方）和共识层（权益证明机制所在的位置）的更新。

预计在 2025 年第一季度实施，其中一些 EIP 可能在升级实施的过程中因某种原因取消。

4⃣对应的 EIP 有哪些？

Pectra 升级推出 20 个以太坊改进提案 （EIP），包括 9 个标准 EIP，解决特定特性或功能，以及 1 个 Meta EIP，将 11 个额外的 EIP 捆绑在一起以简化实施。 EIP-2935 – 通过存储最近区块的哈希值来增强验证 Ethereum 历史数据的过程。这是向无状态执行的一步，其中节点不需要存储整个区块链的历史记录，从而进一步提高了网络效率。

EIP-7002 – 允许验证者更灵活地管理其质押的 ETH。借助 EIP-7002，他们可以直接通过其执行层凭证发起提款或部分提款，为新的质押策略和提高流动性开辟了可能性。

EIP-7251 – 将验证者的最大余额从 32 ETH 提高到 2048 ETH。这有助于大型节点运营商整合他们的股份并减少所需的验证者总数。这种简化可以提高网络效率并降低单个节点的计算负担。

EIP-7594 – 引入了 PeerDAS 机制来优化第 2 层 （L2） 解决方案。通过对跨节点的数据可用性进行采样，PeerDAS 可以简化交易处理并增强 L2 网络的可扩展性，最终以更快、更便宜的交易使用户受益。

EIP-7692 – 此 Meta EIP 是 11 个提案的捆绑包，专注于改进以太坊虚拟机 （EVM） 对象格式 （EOF），一种用于表示以太坊智能合约的结构。通过优化这种格式，EIP-7692 旨在使合约部署和执行更快、更高效，使开发人员和用户都受益。

5⃣升级对以太坊有什么好处？

用户体验方面：强调账户抽象，简化以太坊的使用流程，使其更直观和易于访问。引入无缝 gas 支付、批量交易和可定制安全选项，减少交互摩擦，提升 dApp 使用流畅度。(更好用)

开发者体验：EVM 对象格式（EOF）的改进（EIP-7692）为智能合约开发提供了更高效的工具，加快合约执行并降低成本。（更易开发）

可扩展性：尽管未直接解决扩展问题，但 Pectra 通过优化基础设施为未来升级（如 Verkle Tree）铺平道路，提升交易效率。（速度后面会更快）

网络安全：改进验证和确认流程，消除潜在攻击媒介，加强以太坊抵御威胁和漏洞的能力。（更安全）

$btc 

 The trades I am still holding on all timeframes and multi-timeframe plan.

Below an extensive summary of the trades I am still holding and why. This is an execution oriented post, with mild reminders to my plan on how I'm currently positioned for all timeframes.

To the ones who follow me closely, nothing will be new here, but you all like reminders.

It's part of my transparency and good practice, always keeping you up to date of the general positions I am in without oversharing unnecessary details.

I like to frequently remind you since I do trade multiple timeframes. And I always mildly recommend watching multiple timeframes as a form of practice to stay in tune with the market properly, not lose touch, and it allows to keep your plan flexible adhering to the environment we are in, especially with assets of "permanent" accumulation interest.

Macro plan and trades (Monthly/weekly timeframe)

For the monthly timeframe, the plan continues of the ongoing spot accumulation, where we strongly recommended against "DCA-ing", since that never/rarely allows to get enough near the bottom and it doesn't clearly define how much to "DCA", neither does it have proper invalidation.

Our plan is instead to buy 3 batches and adapt dynamically. One early buy, one near the estimated bottom and one confirmation buy.

Since Feb was our early expected bottom time, that was buy 1, in the summer after the 7.12% bounce was buy 2 which beautifully ended up being the bottom so far indeed, and buy 3 waiting for full macro confirmation.

Positional trade: the long (3-Day timeframe or similar)

Then comes one timeframe step down, where we intended to capture the large breakout which took place imo when price aggressively moved above 69k where we took the entry.

I'm still holding that trade even if September turns red, because the trend likely continues imo afterwards, hence why I'm still holding 35% and might increase size again if opportune deep retraces arise.

So despite the confluences of serious resistance 80-83k, it's only local resistance and does not serve a purpose to fully close a trade on the timeframe above.

Swing trade (6-hourly timeframe or similar)

Because that's what the swing trade is for, the short. Detecting resistance, detecting the OHLC, mmd, order flow locally, March 2025 defence, POI etc. On timeframes where a short against the larger trend makes sense.

Acts as a clean hedge against both the positional and macro spot position as well, and is in full alignment with expecting red September where repeated trades or 1 big swing trade of these shorts can be caught, per our stated plan.

Of the current short, still holding 55% waiting for lower.

Scalps (m30 or similar)

Are all trades below that. Trades I share less often, except for the scalp long recently, as a great example of a scalp aiming for those 1000-2000 point moves total. Great trades to take when $btc starts compressing, ranging and getting "boring".

Scalp plan wise, still expecting higher locally as we indeed have been moving before lower.

Final notes

Notice how recently, I was macro spot positioned, positional long, swing short and scalp long, yet all of the trades managed to co-exist and work out and were in alignment with the overall multi-timeframe plan.

That's because the timeframes from macro -> daily/positional -> swing -> scalp are big enough jumps (factor of 12 or similar) to not affect each other.

They also allow to affect each other through bias -> execution when stepping up or down one timeframe.

That brings the beauty of multi timeframe positioning full circle, helps you stay sharp and when the market does something unexpected, still allows you to profit most of the time.

It's imo a myth to align your "personality" with your trading timeframe. Not investing just because you don't have the patience seems like a detrimental issue, or not taking a swing trade while one of the best swing trade opportunities arises, equally.

So with all that said, I disclosed roughly all positions I hold, why and so you know on all timeframes where I expect price to go + actions towards it.

tweets.text:
The trenches are fun, no doubt, and there’s nothing wrong with exploring them. New markets, new structures and new opportunities are part of trading... staying curious and open minded matters. 

The danger is when curiosity turns into FOMO and a hyper gambling state of mind, constantly chasing the next ticker, the next runner, the next 10x because your timeline makes it look like the easiest money in the market.

To consistently make money in the trenches, you probably need some combination of sophisticated systems/software that identify opportunities early, strong position sizing and trade management, the ability to recognise genuine winners and size into them appropriately, or some form of informational advantage that the average participant simply doesn’t have. 

The other side of that equation is being part of the game itself... launching tokens, promoting them, controlling distribution, or having access to flows and information that others don’t.

And realistically, not everything is always what it appears to be. The statistics coming out are hardly surprising... the majority don’t make much, while a relatively small percentage capture most of the upside. 

Social media naturally amplifies the winners, the huge multiples and the overnight success stories, while behind the scenes there can be , teams, insiders, KOL allocations, side wallets, coordinated flows and plenty of questionable practices. 

But that’s part of understanding the game rather than complaining about it. You either understand the environment, develop an edge within it and participate accordingly... or you don’t.

The important part is knowing what you’re actually good at. If your edge is in the trenches, then become exceptional at it... build the systems, understand the flows, learn the participants and specialise in that environment. 

Personally, my edge has always been spot and futures across crypto and global markets... understanding price, positioning, context, risk and recognising when conditions are favourable enough to press. 

That doesn’t mean ignoring new opportunities. Explore them, trade them small, learn from them and remain adaptable... but don’t abandon a proven process because somebody else appears to be making easier money somewhere else. You cannot borrow somebody else’s edge.

The long game is knowing where your statistical edge lies, understanding the conditions in which you perform best and having the patience to let that compound over time. It isn’t particularly viral... nobody gets excited about taking singles, managing risk, sitting out poor conditions and compounding gradually. 

But when you study many of the best traders, including plenty of the Market Wizards, the recurring theme is usually the same... they know what they’re good at, they know when their edge is present and they don’t feel obligated to participate in every game the market offers.

Know your game, know your edge... and be open minded without losing sight of either.

Have a fab weekend!

They said it at $1,000.  
They said it at $10,000.  
And now, at $110,000, they’re still saying it.
